results.title: Gov. Newsom vetoes controversial AI safety bill
results.content: The legislation would have established requirements for companies to prevent their technology from being used for harm. A man in a blue suit and tie looks to his left with a serious expression, set against a blurred, warm-toned background. Gov. Gavin Newsom has vetoed SB 1047, a controversial bill that would have established requirements for artificial intelligence companies to prevent their technology from being used for harm. “I do not believe this is the best approach to protecting the public from real threats posed by the technology,” Newsom wrote Sunday in a veto message (opens in new tab). In a statement Sunday afternoon, he also said it would have been helpful to hear the governor’s input before he killed the bill but that he’s glad to see Newsom acknowledge AI’s risks. But the same day state lawmakers passed the bill, the U.S. government announced (opens in new tab) that it had reached agreements with OpenAI and Anthropic on testing and evaluating the safety of their models.

Title: Zelle: AI Update: California Governor Vetoes AI Safety Bill
# AI Update: California Governor Vetoes AI Safety Bill. California Gov. Gavin Newsom recently vetoed a landmark bill aimed at establishing safety measures for large AI models after the tech industry raised objections, cautioning it could drive AI companies from the state and hinder innovation. The bill would have mandated safety testing for many of the most advanced AI models. Developers of AI software operating in the state would have also needed to outline methods for turning off the AI models, effectively a kill switch. Earlier this month, Newsom told an audience at Dreamforce, an annual conference hosted by software giant Salesforce, that California must lead in regulating AI in the face of federal inaction but that the proposal "can have a chilling effect on the industry.". The proposal, which drew fierce opposition from startups, tech giants and several Democratic House members, could have hurt the homegrown industry by establishing rigid requirements, Newsom said. "While well-intentioned, SB 1047 does not take into account whether an AI system is deployed in high-risk environments, involves critical decision-making or the use of sensitive data," Newsom said in a statement. The United States is already behind Europe in regulating AI to limit risks. The California proposal wasn’t as comprehensive as regulations in Europe, but it would have been a good first step to set guardrails around the rapidly growing technology that is raising concerns about job loss, misinformation, invasions of privacy and automation bias, supporters said. But even with Newsom’s veto, the California safety proposal is inspiring lawmakers in other states to take up similar measures, said Tatiana Rice, deputy director of the Future of Privacy Forum, a nonprofit that works with lawmakers on technology and privacy proposals. Several state agencies, such as the Office of the Attorney General, the Department of Insurance, and the Workforce Commission, have already begun implementing AI and similar programs internally. As Texas lawmakers prepare for the 89th Legislative Session, set to begin in January 2025, their recommendations regarding the proper regulation of AI will likely play an important role in shaping the future of AI governance in the state and throughout the country.

Title: Ceasefires Denied: How U.S. Vetoes Shield Israel and Silence the World
# Ceasefires Denied: How U.S. Vetoes Shield Israel and Silence the World | by Michael Bennett | Medium. # Ceasefires Denied: How U.S. Vetoes Shield Israel and Silence the World. **The Influence of U.S. Veto Power**. Of the roughly 90 vetoes exercised by the U.S., nearly half were used to block resolutions involving Israel. The first instance of U.S. veto power in defense of Israel occurred in 1972 when the U.S. blocked a resolution condemning Israeli attacks on the Lebanese border. At the time, this marked only the second veto in U.S. history, setting a precedent for the decades to come. Over the years, U.S. vetoes have been used to shield Israel from accountability on various issues, ranging from illegal settlements to violations of international humanitarian law. Since October 2023, the U.S. has vetoed four separate UN Security Council resolutions calling for an immediate, unconditional, and permanent ceasefire in Gaza. The U.S. vetoes have not merely been about shielding Israel from criticism. Each veto sends a message, not only to the international community but to those suffering on the ground, that political alliances outweigh the collective responsibility to uphold justice and human rights. The recent U.S. veto of a resolution on November 20, 2024, falsely claimed to omit provisions for hostage releases. At a time when global unity is needed more than ever, the misuse of veto power risks undermining not only peace efforts but the very credibility of the United Nations. The history of U.S. vetoes on the UNSC is more than a series of decisions; it’s a reflection of priorities and alliances that have shaped decades of unrest. results.title: Remote Firmware Update System with Plant Safety Monitoring and State-Preserving Fallback | Embedded systems
results.content:
Title: Remote Firmware Update System with Plant Safety Monitoring and State-Preserving Fallback | Embedded systems
• Reliable remote firmware updates via UART/XMODEM. • Dual-application architecture for resilience. • State-preserving fallback mechanism for operational continuity. • Controller Board: Executes the bootloader and applications, and handles firmware updates. • Bootloader: Manages flash memory, validates applications, handles firmware updates, and orchestrates application switching based on validation and error conditions. • Application 1 (Fallback): Provides reliable operation focused on completing critical tasks even without external signals. • Application 2 (Active): The primary high-performance application that monitors the 1PPS signal for plant safety, processes state transitions, and performs the main system functions. • Application 1 (0x00008000- 0x00017FFF): 64KB for fallback application. • Configuration (0x0003F400- 0x0003FFFF): Configuration space for application information and error handling. • App1 Length (0x0003F400): Size of Application 1 in bytes. • App1 Checksum (0x0003F404): CRC-32 checksum of Application 1. • App2 Length (0x0003F408): Size of Application 2 in bytes. • App2 Checksum (0x0003F40C): CRC-32 checksum of Application 2. • App2 Error Code (0x0003F410): Error code if Application 2 fails. • App2 State (0x0003F414): Last state of Application 2 before failure. This configuration space enables the bootloader to validate applications, track errors, and preserve state information between application failures and recoveries. • Updates application information during firmware updates. • Preserves unrelated configuration when updating a single application. • Manages state preservation for application continuity. • Error Handling: Records current state and error code in flash. • State Recovery: Reads App2’s last state from configuration. • Command Interface: Sends commands to the bootloader and applications. • XMODEM Implementation: Handles file transfers for firmware updates. • 1- Flash Application 1 (Fallback Image). • 2- Flash Application 2 (Active Image). • 3- Proceed to application execution. • Error Handling: Detects and manages transfer failures. • Application 1 Update: Successfully uploaded and validated the fallback application. • Application 2 Update: Successfully uploaded and validated the active application. • Verification: Validated CRC-32 checksum verification of applications. • System Continuity: No loss of critical tasks despite application failures. • A reliable bootloader with comprehensive application validation. • Secure remote firmware update mechanism using XMODEM protocol. • Innovative state-preserving fallback for operational continuity. • Structured flash memory management with configuration space.

results.title: Gavin Newsom Vetoes AI Safety Bill That Was Opposed By Major Tech Companies
results.content: # California Governor Gavin Newsom Vetoes AI Safety Bill: “I Do Not Believe This Is The Best Approach”. #### More Stories By Ted. Governor Gavin Newsom vetoed a major AI safety bill today, saying that it applied “stringent standards to even the most basic functions — so long as a large system deploys it.”. “I do not believe this is the best approach to protecting the public from real threats posed by the technology,” Newsom said in his veto statement. In a statement, Weiner said, “This veto is a missed opportunity for California to once again lead on innovative tech regulation — just as we did around data privacy and net neutrality — and we are all less safe as a result. I do not agree, however, that to keep the public safe, we must settle for a solution that is not informed by an empirical trajectory analysis of Al systems and capabilities.
